logic_text: Supply Includes All Forms Of Supply - Section 7(1)(a)
natural_text: Under GST, supply covers every way of supplying goods or services - such as selling, renting, leasing or bartering - made or agreed to be made, for something in return, by a person as part of business.

logic_text: Supply Included is TRUE when: [Form Of Supply = all of: [Goods Or Services = any of: Supply is of goods, Supply is of services], [Any Form Of Supply = any of: Activity is a sale, Activity is a transfer, Activity is a barter, Activity is an exchange, Activity is grant of licence, Activity is a rental, Activity is a lease, Activity is a disposal, Activity is another form of supply], [Made Or Agreed To Be Made = any of: Supply is made, Supply is agreed to be made]] AND [Conditions Of Supply = all of: Supply is made for consideration, Supply is by a person, Supply is made in course or furtherance of business] -> C_MOS issues PD_TIAS
natural_text: The transaction is a supply under section 7(1)(a) when goods or services are supplied in some form, made or agreed, for something in return, by a person in the course of business.

logic_text: Form Of Supply: all of [Goods Or Services], [Any Form Of Supply], [Made Or Agreed To Be Made]
natural_text: What is supplied, in what form, and that it is made or agreed.

logic_text: Goods Or Services: any of [Supply is of goods], [Supply is of services]
natural_text: The supply is of goods, of services, or of both.

logic_text: Any Form Of Supply: any of [Activity is a sale], [Activity is a transfer], [Activity is a barter], [Activity is an exchange], [Activity is grant of licence], [Activity is a rental], [Activity is a lease], [Activity is a disposal], [Activity is another form of supply]
natural_text: The transaction is one of the listed forms of supply, or another form of supply.

logic_text: Made Or Agreed To Be Made: any of [Supply is made], [Supply is agreed to be made]
natural_text: The supply has been made, or there is an agreement to make it.

logic_text: Conditions Of Supply: all of [Supply is made for consideration], [Supply is by a person], [Supply is made in course or furtherance of business]
natural_text: Something is given in return, by someone identifiable, as part of their business.

logic_text: Supply is of goods
natural_text: What is being supplied is goods.

logic_text: Supply is of services
natural_text: What is being supplied is services.

logic_text: Activity is a sale
natural_text: The transaction is a sale.

logic_text: Activity is a transfer
natural_text: The transaction transfers the goods or services to someone else.

logic_text: Activity is a barter
natural_text: Goods or services are swapped for other goods or services.

logic_text: Activity is an exchange
natural_text: The transaction is an exchange.

logic_text: Activity is grant of licence
natural_text: The transaction grants a licence, for example to use software or a brand.

logic_text: Activity is a rental
natural_text: Something is rented out.

logic_text: Activity is a lease
natural_text: Something is leased out, such as premises or equipment.

logic_text: Activity is a disposal
natural_text: Something is disposed of, such as selling off an asset.

logic_text: Activity is another form of supply
natural_text: The transaction is some other way of supplying goods or services that is not named in the list.

logic_text: Supply is made
natural_text: The supply has actually taken place.

logic_text: Supply is agreed to be made
natural_text: There is an agreement to make the supply, even if it has not happened yet.

logic_text: Supply is made for consideration
natural_text: Something is given in return for the supply, in money or in kind.

logic_text: Supply is by a person
natural_text: Someone identifiable is making the supply.

logic_text: Supply is made in course or furtherance of business
natural_text: The supply is part of the supplier's business or helps it, including side activities connected with it.

logic_text: Subject Of Supply - What is being supplied - goods, services, both or nothing?
natural_text: Whether the transaction supplies goods, services, both or nothing - usually seen from the HSN or SAC codes on the invoice.

logic_text: Transaction Form Of Supply - What is the form of the transaction?
natural_text: How the goods or services change hands - sale, rental, lease, licence, barter and so on - read from the contract or invoice.

logic_text: Supply Made Flag - Has the supply been made?
natural_text: Whether the goods were delivered or the service was performed.

logic_text: Agreement Exists Flag - Is there an agreement to make the supply?
natural_text: Whether a contract or purchase order commits the parties to the supply.

logic_text: Consideration Amount - What consideration is payable or paid?
natural_text: How much money is paid or payable for the supply.

logic_text: Non Monetary Consideration - Is any consideration given in kind?
natural_text: Whether anything other than money is given in return, such as goods or services.

logic_text: Supplier Party Identifier - Who is the supplier?
natural_text: Who is making the supply, as named on the invoice.

logic_text: General Ledger Account - Which ledger account records the transaction?
natural_text: The account in the books where the transaction is recorded.

logic_text: Recipient Type - Who is the recipient?
natural_text: Who receives the supply - a customer, an employee, a director, a related entity or someone else.

logic_text: Is the consideration a genuine payment or only a book adjustment?
natural_text: For a related entity, check that money really changes hands and is not just an entry in the books.

logic_text: Is this a personal transaction routed through the business rather than a business activity?
natural_text: For an employee or director, check that this is really business activity and not a personal deal passed through the company.

logic_text: Transaction is a supply
natural_text: The transaction has already been found to be a supply under GST.

logic_text: Treatment As Goods Or Services - Section 7(1A)
natural_text: Once a transaction is a supply under GST, Schedule II decides whether it is taxed as goods or as services - for example, selling off a business asset is goods, while renting out an office is services.

logic_text: Supply Of Goods is TRUE when: [Transaction is a supply] AND [Activity is listed in Schedule II] AND [Schedule II treats activity as supply of goods] -> C_TOS issues PD_SOG
natural_text: A supply is treated as goods when Schedule II lists it as a goods-type activity, such as passing ownership of goods or transferring or disposing of business assets.

logic_text: Supply Of Services is TRUE when: [Transaction is a supply] AND [Activity is listed in Schedule II] AND [Schedule II treats activity as supply of services] -> C_TOS issues PD_SOS
natural_text: A supply is treated as services when Schedule II lists it as a services-type activity, such as leasing a building, job work on someone else's goods, developing software or a works contract.

logic_text: Activity is listed in Schedule II
natural_text: The activity is one of those named in Schedule II, such as a lease, job work, transfer of business assets or a works contract.

logic_text: Schedule II treats activity as supply of goods
natural_text: Schedule II classes this activity as goods - for example ownership of goods passes to the buyer, or business assets are sold off.

logic_text: Schedule II treats activity as supply of services
natural_text: Schedule II classes this activity as services - for example renting property, licensing intellectual property, job work, or letting goods be used without passing ownership.

logic_text: Schedule II Entry Code - Which Schedule II entry, if any, describes this transaction?
natural_text: Which Schedule II category the transaction falls into - for example lease of a building, transfer of ownership, job work, or none - usually found in the contract, lease deed or invoice description.

logic_text: Immovable Property Involved - Does the transaction involve land or a building?
natural_text: Whether land or a building is part of the transaction, usually seen in the contract or the asset register.

logic_text: Is this a works contract for immovable property, or a sale of goods with incidental installation?
natural_text: For work on land or a building, check whether it is a works contract (services) or simply a sale of goods with some installation (goods).

logic_text: Does the transaction pass title in the goods, or only a right to use them?
natural_text: Check whether the customer actually becomes the owner of the goods or only gets to use them - ownership points to goods, use only points to services.
